help.favorites_text: The star keeps a log as a favourite — next to the picker or right in the list. Favourites come first in the list and as buttons below it. Out of the box the syslog, kernel, Docker, messenger, Mr. Backupsy's latest run, Kopia and Jack Streamer's log are favourites; "↺ Favourites out of the box" brings them back. Kept in this browser.
help.source_text: Around the office (messenger, Mr. Backupsy's runs, Jack Streamer's runs), Unraid's own logs (syslog, kernel, VMs, web UI, Samba …), what every User Script printed last, and every container's logs.
help.live: Like tail -f: every two seconds I fetch what was added. Scroll up to read in peace — I only jump to the end again when you're at the bottom.
help.only: Shows only the lines that sound like an error (red) or a warning (yellow) — by the same rules as my tour (see «What I count»). Whether something is really bad, I don't know.
help.colours: Red: sounds like an error. Yellow: sounds like a warning. The filter marks what you look for; a line from my tour is marked, too.
help.safe_text: I only read, and only from a fixed list: /var/log lives in RAM, nothing wakes a disk. Logs can hold sensitive things — only who is logged in to Unraid sees them.
help.tour_text: On a tour I walk through every log on my list: how full /var/log is and which files there are biggest, how big every container's log is and whether Docker limits it — and which lines sound like an error or a warning. In the background, a few seconds; I change nothing and wake no disk. «Follow live» and «Show in the log» open the reader below.
help.counted_text: A line that names its own level (level=warn, [ERROR], | INFO |, PHP Warning …) goes by that name. Every other line by its words: error, fail, fatal, panic, segfault, denied, an exit code … is an error; warning, timeout, retry a warning; in the kernel log also what the kernel marks itself. «0 errors», «errors: 0» and rsync's lists of file names don't count. I only recognise words — a warning in a log isn't always a problem, and not every problem says so.
help.rules_text: Unraid's syslog I also sort by rules: first your own («Set up»), then the ones I was given (from Enhanced Log): disks, network, file systems, array, logins, system … — the first rule that fits decides. «Disks» is Enhanced Log's «Drive Related» and catches USB and SCSI lines, too. My tile «Syslog» shows the counts and, per kind, the newest lines; a label shows only one kind. Without a recent tour I sort the syslog's newest lines at once. What they call an error counts as an error, a minor issue at least as a warning, noise («Noise») neither; never less than my words found. The reader colours the syslog the same way and gives each line its kind's edge.
help.grouped_text: Lines that only differ in times, numbers, IDs or addresses are one entry: how often, first and last seen, and the newest of them as it stands. A click unfolds it; «Show in the log» opens it in the reader, at that line.
help.since_text: Since my previous tour — on my first one, the last 24 hours (as far as the lines carry a time). Of a file at most the newest 4 MB, of a container at most 3000 lines; containers only while they run.
help.space_text: A small RAM disk (128 MB on Unraid) for Unraid's own logs — when it is full, nothing more can be written there. Over 60 % I tell the team lead, over 80 % it is on his «Still to do». The containers' own logs lie elsewhere, in Docker's folder; how big they may get is set under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Docker⟧ → ⟦Docker LOG rotation⟧.
check.varlog_how: /var/log is a small RAM disk for Unraid's own logs. When it is full, nothing more gets logged — and whatever goes wrong then leaves no trace. Ms. Protocolli's tour shows which files there are biggest and how fast they grow; usually one program writes the same line again and again — fix or stop it. A single file can be emptied in a terminal with truncate -s 0 <file>; a reboot empties /var/log.
fit.yes: Ms. Protocolli would love to come: "I can't do anything, but I can read everything out!"

help.mine_text: Your own rules for Unraid's syslog: a regular expression (without slashes, case doesn't matter) and a kind. They come before the rules I was given, in their order — the first that fits decides, as in Enhanced Log. A rule is checked before I keep it: it must be readable, must not fit every line and must not run away on long lines.
help.hide_text: Lines whose message contains a text of this list count as noise — never an error or a warning, not listed under «Syslog». They stay in the syslog: I only hide them in my view, I never change the syslog.
help.el_text: While Enhanced Log is installed I read its settings (read only): its custom rules become rules of mine, its syslog filter texts I hide in my view. The first time on my own, later what is new on «Take over». When you remove Enhanced Log, its settings go with it — and its filter: those lines are written into the syslog again.
errors.logs_mine_form: Line breaks or control characters can't be in it.
errors.logs_mine_regex: That isn't a regular expression I can read (a «/» needs a «\» before it).
errors.logs_mine_every: It fits every line — that would put the whole syslog under one kind.
errors.logs_mine_slow: It runs away on long lines — please make it simpler.
errors.logs_mine_browser: It uses something only the server reads (inline flags, \A, \z, possessive quantifiers …) — the page would colour differently.
errors.logs_mine_full: I keep at most {n} — remove one first.
errors.logs_el_gone: Enhanced Log's settings aren't there any more.
time.label: Time
time.clock_bad: A time as hh:mm, 24 hours (07:30, 18:05) — otherwise the whole day counts.
saved.label: Saved filters:
saved.save_hint: Keeps what is set now under a name — on the server, for every browser. It only applies when you click it.
saved.save_text: I keep for this list: {what}. It only applies when you click its button — never by itself. A time like «Last hour» then counts from that click.
saved.delete_text: Only the saved filter «{name}» goes — the logs and what the list shows stay as they are.
help.time_text: Above every list whose rows have a time: the last hour, the last 24 hours, today, since the server started — or «From … to …» with a day and a time (24 hours; either end may stay empty). A kind of line («×n») counts by its newest line, a file and a container's log by their last write, the lines read by their own time (a line without one by the line before it). What has no time fits no time filter.
help.saved_text: «Save filter…» keeps what a list's bar has set — words, labels, «Errors & warnings only», the time — under a name. I keep them on the server: every browser and the phone see the same. A click on its button sets it; none ever applies by itself, the page always opens with everything. «Last hour» stays the last hour from the click. Rename and delete with «⋯».
